condition: Colorectal cancer screening — average-to-moderate risk, African-Caribbean
permutationLabel: No symptoms; father CRC at 58; no national programme
summary: 47-year-old St Lucian man of African-Caribbean descent, asymptomatic, father had colorectal cancer at 58, asks about screening. There is no national bowel screening programme in Saint Lucia; USPSTF 2021 starts average-risk screening at 45; ACG 2021 recommends colonoscopy from 40, 5-yearly, for one FDR diagnosed < 60. BSG 2020 would not add colonoscopy for one FDR diagnosed ≥ 50.

inputs.hpi: No bowel symptoms. Father diagnosed with colorectal cancer at 58 (alive, treated in Martinique). Has never had a FIT or colonoscopy. Read that bowel cancer is rising in younger Caribbean men. Hypertension, obesity.
comorbidities: Family history of colorectal cancer (father, age 58)
inputs.socialHistory: Bus driver. Non-smoker. Diet high in processed meat.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Colorectal cancer screening — family history of colorectal cancer
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Asymptomatic, age 47, one first-degree relative with colorectal cancer at 58. Colorectal cancer screening discussion.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Over-triage: the words "colorectal cancer" in the family-history comorbidity trigger "Possible malignancy" (priority) → same_day_call for an asymptomatic screening request.

mustInclude.note: USPSTF 2021 / ACG 2021: average-risk screening from 45. ACG 2021: one FDR with CRC diagnosed < 60 (father at 58) → colonoscopy from age 40 (or 10 years before the relative’s age at diagnosis), repeated every 5 years — so he is overdue on the ACG reading. BSG 2020 (UK) would not add colonoscopic surveillance for a single FDR diagnosed ≥ 50. The practice’s policy needs the surgeon’s decision. Not observable in the web harness: the dashboard feeds the Family History field (ClinicalPromptsStrip familyHistory) to computeClinicalPrompts, but the vignette schema has no family-history input, so web-runner passes []. In the dashboard the "FHx colorectal cancer, age 35–49" prompt would probably add a colonoscopy. Needs a familyHistory input in the schema and both runners. Without a family history there is no screening prompt before 50: the average-risk "colorectal_screen" prompt starts at age 50 (USPSTF 2021 and ACG 2021: 45) and offers FOBT every 2 years rather than annual FIT.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for colorectal cancer
guideline.section: Screen adults aged 45–49 (grade B) and 50–75 (grade A)
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for colorectal cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2021;325:1965–1977.

guideline.name: ACG clinical guidelines — colorectal cancer screening
guideline.section: Average risk: start at 45; one FDR with CRC or advanced adenoma diagnosed < 60, or two FDRs: colonoscopy from 40 (or 10 years before the youngest affected relative) every 5 years
guideline.citation: Shaukat A, Kahi CJ, Burke CA, et al. ACG clinical guidelines: colorectal cancer screening 2021. Am J Gastroenterol. 2021;116:458–479.

guideline.name: BSG/ACPGBI/UKCGG guidelines — management of hereditary colorectal cancer
guideline.section: Moderate-risk family history thresholds (one FDR < 50, or two FDRs) for UK colonoscopic surveillance
guideline.citation: Monahan KJ, Bradshaw N, Dolwani S, et al. Guidelines for the management of hereditary colorectal cancer from the British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG)/Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland (ACPGBI)/United Kingdom Cancer Genetics Group (UKCGG). Gut. 2020;69:411–444.

rationale: Screening encounter in the Saint Lucian context (no organised programme; opportunistic screening). All expectations are quality: guideline bodies differ on the FDR ≥ 50 case and the practice’s policy is not written down.

authoring.author: Claude (colorectal/anorectal cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Citations verified: false until checked against the source.
